reviews.body:
Please add integration tests in tests/integration, modeled on `ListObjects_url_encoding`, and register them in group-tests.go (test group + name map):
- `ListObjectVersions_url_encoding` (versioning group): put `a+ b.txt`, `dir a/obj`, and `del me+` with a delete marker. List with `EncodingType: url, Delimiter: "/"` and assert `EncodingType`, the version and delete-marker keys (`a%2B+b.txt`, `del+me%2B`) and the CommonPrefix `dir+a/`. Add a page with `Prefix`/`KeyMarker` containing "+ " and `MaxKeys: 1` to cover encoded Prefix/KeyMarker/NextKeyMarker, and check that `gibberish` returns InvalidArgument.
- `ListMultipartUploads_url_encoding`: the same with uploads (` x(test)+` → `+x%28test%29%2B`, `dir b/up` → CP `dir+b/`), including Prefix/KeyMarker/NextKeyMarker and the invalid value.
This matters more than usual: aws-cli/boto3 send `encoding-type=url` on every ListObjectVersions call and decode the response, so this PR changes the wire output for those clients.

The bats tests for these issues are still skipped: tests/test_rest_list_multipart_uploads.sh:158-160 and :184-186 (#2156), and tests/test_rest_list_object_versions.sh:73-75 and :81-83 (#2169). They only check keys and errors, so they should pass with this fix. Please drop the `skip` blocks.

review_comments.body: `ListVersionsResult.EncodingType` (s3response/s3response.go:593) has no `omitempty`, so every ListObjectVersions response without `encoding-type` still carries an empty `<EncodingType></EncodingType>`. S3 omits the element unless it was requested. The #2169 thread calls this out, and ListObjects/V2 got the same fix in a7b91dd0. Please add `xml:",omitempty"` there, plus a unit test that marshals an unencoded result and asserts the element is absent. The Go SDK can't tell empty from absent, so an SDK test won't catch this.

`urlEncodeString` goes through a pointer round trip (`*urlEncodeKeyName(&name)`) and sits apart from the helper it wraps. Inverting them is cleaner: `urlEncodeString(name string) string { return s3KeyNameEscaper.Replace(url.QueryEscape(name)) }`, with `urlEncodeKeyName` as a nil-safe wrapper around it. Please keep both next to each other above `urlEncodeCommonPrefixes`.

These four inline copy-and-encode loops(1356, 1377, 1385 lines) break the pattern the file already uses (`urlEncodeObjectKeys`, `urlEncodeCommonPrefixes`). Please extract `urlEncodeVersionKeys`, `urlEncodeDeleteMarkerKeys`, `urlEncodeUploadKeys` and `urlEncodeUploadPrefixes` (for `[]s3response.CommonPrefix`) next to them, so both exported functions read as flat field assignments like `URLEncodeListObjectsResult`.
Minor: ListObjects/V2 in this file return early on a backend error and then encode. `if err == nil && encodingType != ""` works, but please use the same early return in both handlers for consistency.

The leading space in `" x(test)+"` breaks this test on the azure backend. The backend stores the key raw in the `x-ms-meta-Objname` header, HTTP trims the leading space, and the shared-key signature no longer matches: CreateMultipartUpload returns 403 AuthorizationFailure (reproduced on main against Azurite). azurite.yml runs `full-flow --azure`, which includes TestListMultipartUploads. Please drop the leading space, e.g. `"x (test)+"`, and expect `"x+%28test%29%2B"` on line 887. That still covers space, parentheses and `+`.
This test only checks an `s3response` struct tag, so it belongs in s3response/s3response_test.go.

comments.body: This won't automatically run in continuous integration without approval. A member of the Versity organization must allow it.

Thanks for the detailed review. Pushed a commit addressing it: `urlEncodeString`/`urlEncodeKeyName` inverted and placed above `urlEncodeCommonPrefixes`; extracted `urlEncodeVersionKeys`, `urlEncodeDeleteMarkerKeys`, `urlEncodeUploadKeys`, `urlEncodeUploadPrefixes`; `xml:",omitempty"` on `ListVersionsResult.EncodingType` with a marshal unit test; early return on backend error in both handlers; new integration tests `ListObjectVersions_url_encoding` and `ListMultipartUploads_url_encoding` (registered in group-tests.go); and the `skip` blocks for #2156/#2169 removed from the bats tests (not run locally, no bats environment).
